messages:
Alex Carter: Quick follow-up to the RFC I posted earlier — namespace flattening for telemetry keys. TL;DR: collapse a couple of high-cardinality span labels into a small, predictable keyspace and push service-level metadata to the envelope. Goal: reduce index cardinality, make cost attribution simpler, and improve query performance. Looking for tradeoffs and a rollout plan.

Meera Patel: Can you sketch the concrete change? curious about how this affects metric/tag queries and per-tenant cost breakdowns.

Alex Carter: Sure — example before/after:

```json
// before
{
  "span.service": "payments-v2",
  "span.name": "authorize_card",
  "span.version": "2024-11-02",
  "tenant_id": "acct_42"
}

// after
{
  "service_name": "payments",
  "span_name": "authorize_card",
  "service_tier": "v2",          // normalized, low-cardinality
  "tenant_id": "acct_42",
  "envelope_meta": { "raw_version": "2024-11-02" } // stored separately for infrequent lookups
}
```

Alex Carter: The idea is to normalize service strings (strip build hashes, timestamps), collapse minor variant tokens into a small enum (service_tier), and keep the noisy raw fields in an attachable meta blob that lives in cold storage/index. That keeps normal queries fast and cost attribution clean.

Jamal Ortiz: Two immediate concerns: (1) backcompat for existing dashboards/alerts that use raw span.service, (2) how to perform ad-hoc forensic queries that need the original raw value.

Sasha Kim: +1 on Jamal's concerns. We rely on the raw version field in a couple of incident playbooks to correlate deployments with regressions. If we push it to cold store, we need a clear quick-path for on-call.

Alex Carter: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: (A) add a lightweight compatibility mapping layer in the query service that rewrites legacy predicates to the new flattened keys for the first ~6 months, (B) keep a TTL'd alias field "legacy_key" that is populated at ingest for N days to allow dashboards to continue running, and (C) preserve raw values in envelope_meta but with longer lookup latency.

Meera Patel: For cost attribution: we should ensure the billing pipeline can map old service strings to normalized service_name during migration. I suggest emitting a lineage event when a legacy_key->service_name mapping is created so the cost joiner can consume it.

Jamal Ortiz: Rollout phases I propose:
1) Opt-in ingest adapter (users can select legacy vs flattened keys)
2) Query alias layer + UA (metrics & dashboards still query legacy by default)
3) Backfill normalized index for 30d hot window
4) Flip default to flattened and phase out legacy_key

Sasha Kim: What about retention? If raw_version stays around but in cold storage, how long do we keep it? Some debugging requires >90 days occasionally.

Alex Carter: Suggestion: keep envelope_meta for 365d but mark it cold (slower queries, higher cost), keep legacy_key for 30d, and keep the flattened keys as source of truth for fast queries. We can revisit based on usage metrics.

Meera Patel: We should also update the attribution pipeline to tag every event with normalized_service during ingest so downstream cost joiner has a deterministic key even mid-migration. That prevents partial attribution gaps.

infra-bot: :gear: deployment queued for branch namespace-flatten-v2 — config change to ingest-adapter staged in feature environment.

Jamal Ortiz: One more operational note: add a migration metric (normalized_mapped_ratio) to track how many incoming events get normalized vs stay legacy. We can gate flips on that metric.

Sasha Kim: We'll need runbook updates and at least one oncall drill where we exercise querying envelope_meta (cold path) to ensure latency is acceptable.

Alex Carter: Action items (owners):
- Alex: write migration plan doc with phases and expected timelines
- Meera: add lineage event spec and update cost joiner contract
- Jamal: implement query alias + migration metric in query-service
- Sasha: draft runbook & cold-path drill

Meera Patel: 👍 ack, will start the lineage spec today.

Jamal Ortiz: I'll prototype the alias in the query-service next sprint, will post PR link here.

Sasha Kim: I'll draft the runbook and schedule the drill with oncall.

Alex Carter: Thanks everyone — I'll post the migration doc and a short compatibility checklist by EOD tomorrow. If anyone has objections to the phases above, reply here. Otherwise I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the concrete steps. :rocket:
